extra.message: User-controlled todo content (req.body.content) is matched against an image regex and the captured URL is concatenated into a shell command passed to child_process.exec('identify ' + url). An attacker can post content such as '![alt text](https://x/y.png;touch ./public/p0wned "c")' so the captured value contains shell metacharacters, resulting in OS command injection / remote code execution.

In the login handler, req.body.username and req.body.password are passed directly into a Mongoose User.find() query without type validation. Because bodyParser.json() is enabled globally, an attacker can send JSON like {"username":"admin@snyk.io","password":{"$gt":""}}; the $gt operator is interpreted by MongoDB, bypassing the password check and authenticating as any known user (NoSQL injection / authentication bypass).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /import route extracts an attacker-supplied ZIP (AdmZip 0.4.7) with zip.extractAllTo('/tmp/extracted_files', true) without validating any archive entry names. A crafted archive containing entries such as '../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys' is written outside the target directory (Zip-Slip), enabling arbitrary file write on the server (CWE-22). No authentication is required on this route.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: The /about_new handler passes the raw query string parameter req.query.device into a dust.js template (views/about_new.dust) where it is interpolated inside the {@if cond="'{device}'=='Desktop'"} directive. The dustjs-linkedin engine evaluates that interpolated condition; when device is supplied as an array (?device[]=...), the engine's escaping is bypassed and the injected expression is evaluated server-side (see exploits/dustjs-exploits.sh), leading to template code injection / RCE.

chat.add merges the attacker-controlled req.body.message into a fresh object with lodash's _.merge() (lodash 4.17.4). lodash.merge recursively copies __proto__/constructor keys, so an unprivileged chat user can send {"message":{"__proto__":{"canDelete":true}}} to pollute Object.prototype.canDelete. Because chat.delete() checks !user.canDelete, the low-privileged 'user' account then passes the check and can delete messages, i.e. prototype pollution leading to an authorization/privilege escalation bypass.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

extra.message: The login page renders the user-controlled query parameter redirectPage (routes/index.js exports.login: req.query.redirectPage) directly into a hidden input value with the EJS unescaped-output tag <%- redirectPage %>. An attacker can craft /login?redirectPage=" onload="alert(1) (or similar) to execute arbitrary script in the victim's session (reflected XSS).

The login POST handler takes redirectPage from req.body.redirectPage and, after a successful login, passes it to res.redirect(redirectPage) without validating that it is a relative path. A user can be redirected to an arbitrary external URL (e.g. https://evil.example) after login, enabling phishing (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Stored todo content (attacker-controlled via the unauthenticated POST /create route) is rendered with <%- marked(new String(todo.content)) %>. The <%- tag outputs unescaped HTML and the markdown is run through marked 0.3.5 whose 'sanitize' option only strips HTML tags and does not neutralize javascript: URLs in generated links (confirmed by exploits/marked-exploit.sh, e.g. [x](javascript&#58this;alert(1))). Any user visiting the home page triggers the stored XSS.

The /users endpoints perform no authentication or authorization (the comment on lines 13-15 explicitly states auth is 'not implemented'). Any anonymous caller can GET user records from the MySQL users table. Combined with prototype pollution of Object.prototype.where (via POST /users), the fixed repo.find({id:1}) call can be made to return arbitrary user records (IDOR / enumeration of all accounts).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /users copies the client-supplied role field straight into the persisted record (user.role = req.body.role). Because there is no server-side check, an attacker can create a user with role 'admin', escalating privileges to the seeded admin account (mass assignment / broken access control).

user.address is assigned an unvalidated nested object from the request body and then persisted via TypeORM's repo.save(user). A payload such as {"name":"a","address":{"__proto__":{"where":{"id":"2"}}}} is merged by TypeORM and pollutes Object.prototype.where; the polluted 'where' then overrides the hard-coded {id:1} criteria in the GET handler, letting an anonymous attacker read any account (see exploits/prototype-pollution-typeorm.md).

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /create stores the request body content without any type/length validation into a Mongoose field typed as Buffer. If content is sent as a number (e.g. {"content":800}), parse() returns it unchanged and Mongoose 4.2.4 casts the number into a Buffer of that size without initializing it. The raw buffer is then sent back base64-encoded to the client (todo.content.toString('base64')) and rendered on the page, disclosing uninitialized server heap memory (see exploits/mongoose-exploits.sh). Very large numbers also allow trivial memory-exhaustion DoS.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: On startup the app seeds a real admin account with the hard-coded password 'SuperSecretPassword' (username 'admin@snyk.io') whenever it does not exist. This default credential ships in source code, so anyone can log in to the /admin area. Passwords are also stored in plaintext (Schema field password: String) with no hashing.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: MySQL connection credentials are hard-coded in source (username 'root' / password 'root', database 'acme'). Hard-coded database credentials allow anyone with source access to connect directly to the database, and 'logging: true' additionally logs all queries.

The express-session signing secret is hard-coded to the well-known value 'keyboard cat' with no rotation and no secure/httpOnly cookie options. An attacker who knows the secret can forge session cookies (connect.sid) and set req.session.loggedIn=1 to bypass the isLoggedIn gate for the /admin and /account_details routes.

A secret token ('SECRET_TOKEN_f8ed84e8f41e4146403dd4a6bbcea5e418d23a9') is hard-coded in the source and then written to the console on every startup, exposing it in logs and to any process/user able to read application output.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
